evidence.claim: Rapamycin partially preserved neuroblast number in a 2026 fly SAC-loss model; the model depleted bub3/rod, not BUB1B. Genetic TOR/autophagy interventions did not restore progeny counts or brain size.
evidence.locator: Results pp10-14, treatment methods pp16-17; Fig6 and discussion of Supplementary Fig6C; supplement image not independently inspected
evidence.genotype: Neural bub3/rod depletion; complex aneuploidy; not BUB1B allele pair
evidence.intervention_comparator: Rapamycin versus DMSO; genetic Atg1/Rheb/Tor perturbations
evidence.exposure: 40 micromolar in food for approximately 48 h; DMSO 0.4%; tissue exposure not measured
evidence.endpoint: Neuroblast number; separate genetic-intervention progeny and brain-size endpoints
evidence.effect_magnitude: Neuroblast rescue reported; no demonstrated functional tissue rescue from rapamycin; not reduced segregation errors
evidence.replication_statistics: Paper reports at least two independent replicates per genotype; supplement-specific raw statistics not reanalyzed
evidence.target_specificity: Convergent genetic TOR/autophagy interventions; not BUB1B-specific
evidence.negative_conflicting: Preserving aneuploid stem cells may not preserve productive progeny and may retain premalignant cells

evidence.claim: In the same fly SAC-loss study, genetic mitochondrial chaperone or ROS-scavenger overexpression restored brain size more successfully than TOR/autophagy manipulation.
evidence.locator: Fig7; results pp13-14; Hsp60/Hsp60c, Sod2 and GTPx-1 interventions
evidence.endpoint: Mitochondrial reporters, neuroblast/progeny counts, brain size
evidence.effect_magnitude: Partial neuroblast rescue with reported full brain-size restoration; chromosome correction not shown
evidence.target_specificity: Multiple genetic perturbations and mitochondrial/proteostasis reporters
evidence.negative_conflicting: Microcephaly not supplied for child; no muscle/renal transfer or approved antioxidant equivalence established; apoptosis blockade especially concerning in cancer

evidence.claim: BubR1-low mice were more sensitive to experimentally imposed oxidative stress; this does not demonstrate spontaneous oxidative injury or antioxidant rescue in this case.
evidence.intervention_comparator: Potassium bromate versus water; WT comparison
evidence.exposure: 2 g/L potassium bromate, 16 weeks, experimental oxidant challenge
evidence.effect_magnitude: Higher mortality under oxidant challenge; no antioxidant treatment performed

evidence.claim: Macrolides have readthrough evidence in reporter and ApcMin/+ mouse studies; this is not BUB1B rescue, and microbiome effects complicate tumor outcomes.
evidence.locator: Both PubMed abstracts; full-text downloads unavailable/invalid; corrections 10.1007/s00109-016-1394-3 and 10.1016/j.biopha.2023.115082 identified but corrective content unavailable
evidence.model_species: Mammalian reporters and ApcMin/+ mouse intestine
evidence.genotype: Other nonsense alleles; no BUB1B model
evidence.exposure: Mouse drinking-water concentrations reported, but no free tissue exposure or BUB1B effective concentration established; not converted to child dose
evidence.endpoint: Longer APC, downstream signaling and intestinal tumors
evidence.effect_magnitude: Reported protein restoration and tumor suppression; no precise magnitude used while corrections remain unresolved
evidence.replication_statistics: Two distinct study programs; neither replicates exact BUB1B allele rescue
evidence.negative_conflicting: Apc allele, microbiome and intestinal exposure do not validate systemic BUB1B readthrough
evidence.funding_conflicts: 2016 authors include Bioblast Pharma affiliations; 2023 authors declare no known competing financial interests

evidence.claim: Arimoclomol altered HSF1/HSP70 and lysosomal phenotypes in NPC models, but its clinical NPC mechanism remains unknown in the FDA label.
evidence.locator: Results arimoclomol section; Fig6 and discussion; PMC author manuscript
evidence.model_species: NPC patient fibroblasts and Npc1-null mice
evidence.exposure: Cell exposure-response 24h; mouse treatment 3-7 weeks of age; no BUB1B target exposure
evidence.endpoint: HSF1/HSP70, lysosomal storage and neurological phenotypes
evidence.effect_magnitude: Context-dependent improvement; not mutant BUBR1 stabilization
evidence.target_specificity: Orthogonal HSP70 interventions but no BUBR1 epistasis
evidence.negative_conflicting: E48 found no arimoclomol response in another NPC1 fibroblast study
evidence.funding_conflicts: Orphazyme-affiliated investigators; not independent of commercial development

evidence.claim: A later NPC1 fibroblast study found no HSP70 induction or cholesterol-storage correction with arimoclomol up to 0.5 mM; broad chaperone amplification cannot be presumed.
evidence.locator: Published PMC results/abstract; earlier preprint PDF also encountered, not counted separately
evidence.intervention_comparator: Arimoclomol versus HSP90 inhibitors/HSP70 expression controls
evidence.exposure: Up to 0.5 mM; not a proposed achievable concentration
evidence.effect_magnitude: No correction in tested context; not a BUB1B null result
evidence.negative_conflicting: Different from E47; assay/cell-state or exposure differences not resolved
evidence.funding_conflicts: Authors declare no conflict of interest in published PubMed record

evidence.claim: Niacin replenished NAD in adults with mitochondrial myopathy; BUBR1 abundance, SIRT2-selective activation and childhood MVA efficacy were not established.
evidence.locator: PubMed abstract; publisher full text inaccessible; correction identified, content not reviewed
evidence.model_species: Adults with mitochondrial myopathy and matched controls
evidence.intervention_comparator: Niacin supplementation in patients and controls; not placebo randomized efficacy evidence
evidence.exposure: Adult intervention with differing patient/control duration; no child dose or BUBR1 effective exposure derived
evidence.effect_magnitude: NAD replenishment and muscle changes reported; some anemia tendency; no quantitative effect used without full methods/correction
evidence.negative_conflicting: Low muscle bulk does not establish mitochondrial myopathy or NAD deficiency
evidence.funding_conflicts: NAD-assay patent and NR-related IP/company interests reported in PubMed record

evidence.claim: Azithromycin tablets/oral suspension are approved antibacterial medicines with pediatric indication-specific age limits; no readthrough approval.
evidence.exposure: Approved antibacterial exposure; chronic readthrough exposure not established
evidence.effect_magnitude: Pediatric otitis/CAP from 6 months and pharyngitis from 2 years; QT/torsades, liver injury, GI effects, hearing-related interactions and neonatal pyloric-stenosis warning

evidence.claim: Arimoclomol capsules are US-approved with miglustat for neurological NPC from age2; clinical mechanism unknown; creatinine can rise without GFR decline and OCT2 interactions matter.
evidence.locator: Indications, warnings, interactions; mechanism section retrieved in targeted search
evidence.exposure: NPC exposure established; rescuing BUBR1 exposure unknown
evidence.effect_magnitude: Initial approval 2024-09-20; diarrhea/decreased weight, hypersensitivity, OCT2 effects; renal assessment cannot rely on creatinine alone under exposure

evidence.claim: Prescription niacin ER is a US-approved lipid-lowering medicine distinct from NMN/NR supplements; pediatric safety/effectiveness <=16 not established.
evidence.locator: Macleods ANDA label; indications, warnings and pediatric section; inactive 2012 repackaged Niaspan record not used as current availability proof
evidence.exposure: Lipid indication exposure; no BUBR1 rescue threshold
evidence.effect_magnitude: Hepatic injury, flushing, glucose/urate effects, muscle injury with statins, renal caution; formulations not interchangeable

evidence.claim: CPIC guideline: aminoglycosides (including amikacin) are relatively contraindicated in carriers of MT-RNR1 variants m.1555A>G, m.1494C>T or m.1095T>C, which sharply raise aminoglycoside-induced hearing-loss risk; there is insufficient evidence that any class member is safer.
evidence.locator: Abstract and therapeutic recommendations; MT-RNR1 12S rRNA mechanism and class-wide guidance
evidence.intervention_comparator: Aminoglycoside use stratified by MT-RNR1 genotype
evidence.exposure: Shortest-possible aminoglycoside course with drug and ototoxicity monitoring if unavoidable
evidence.effect_magnitude: Strong recommendation to avoid aminoglycosides in carriers unless infection severity outweighs permanent hearing-loss risk; no intra-class safety ranking supported
evidence.negative_conflicting: Guideline concerns ototoxicity, not BUB1B readthrough efficacy; does not establish amikacin read-through of p.Leu737*

evidence.claim: BUBR1/Bub1b is an autophagy substrate degraded via lysosomes preferentially in senescence; hydroxychloroquine raised BUBR1 only in late-passage senescent cells, whereas the autophagy inducer everolimus lowered it.
evidence.locator: Fig6 and results: HCQ/3-MA/MG132/everolimus immunoblots; BubR1-LC3 interaction and xLIR motif
evidence.model_species: Human Wharton-jelly MSCs and mouse tissues
evidence.genotype: Replicative senescence model; not supplied BUB1B variants
evidence.intervention_comparator: HCQ, 3-MA, MG132, everolimus versus untreated; early versus late passage
evidence.exposure: HCQ 100 micromolar for 2 h to block lysosomal proteolysis; not a clinical exposure
evidence.endpoint: BubR1/Bub1b protein level and autophagic/lysosomal degradation
evidence.effect_magnitude: BubR1 increased by HCQ only in senescent (late-passage) cells; everolimus reduced it; degradation-blocking, not increased synthesis
evidence.target_specificity: Convergent autophagy inhibitors (HCQ, 3-MA) and proteasome control (MG132); LC3 co-IP
evidence.orthogonal_validation: Immunoblot, co-IP, confocal colocalisation and LIR-motif alignment
evidence.negative_conflicting: Effect is senescence-specific; chronic autophagy inhibition carries its own risks and does not restore function

evidence.claim: Olaparib (Lynparza) is an FDA-approved PARP inhibitor indicated for BRCA/HRR-mutated ovarian, breast, pancreatic and prostate cancers selected by a companion diagnostic; there is no rhabdomyosarcoma or BUB1B indication.
evidence.locator: Indications and usage; warnings 5.2/5.4; initial US approval 2014
evidence.intervention_comparator: Olaparib 300 mg twice daily per label; companion-diagnostic selected
evidence.exposure: Established oncology exposure; no RMS or constitutional-cell window
evidence.effect_magnitude: Myelodysplastic syndrome/AML, pneumonitis and venous thromboembolism warnings; pediatric effectiveness not established
evidence.negative_conflicting: Chromosomal instability is not homologous-recombination deficiency; a PARP indication does not follow from BUB1B loss alone
